### Observed differences

- The order between the five-activity block A30/A31/A36/A37/A38 and A21/A22 flipped completely. In the earlier window, each block activity ran before A21 and before A22 in 100 in 100 traces; in the later window, A21 and A22 each ran before every block activity in about 99–100 in 100 traces. The activities still co-occurred in essentially all traces in both windows, so participation itself did not change. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010]
- Successors around this block were rewired. In the earlier window A20's outgoing transitions spread almost evenly over the five block activities (about 19–23% each); in the later window about 99–100 in 100 of them go to A22. A21 led to A25 in all earlier-window transitions but now spreads over the five block activities (about 16–23% each), with A25 nearly gone. Each block activity lost A22 as a successor (from about 18–22% to about 0) and gained A25 (from 0 to about 18–23%), while transitions among the five themselves stayed similar. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007]
- Event positions shifted consistently with this: A22's mean relative position moved from about 0.52 to 0.39 and A21's from 0.65 to 0.52, while the five block activities moved later, from about 0.43–0.44 to about 0.60. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007]
- Close succession disappeared: the ordered pairs "A20 before a block activity" and "a block activity before A22" within five steps occurred in 200 of 200 earlier-window traces but only 1 of 200 later-window traces. The later-window lag profiles rest on a single trace each and are weak on their own. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]
- The elapsed time between consecutive completions shortened on three activity pairs: A09→A10 fell from about 1.0 h to 0.5 h on average, A11→A10 from about 1.0 h to 0.5 h (125 vs 110 observations), and A24→A28 from about 1.0 h to essentially zero (median 0 h in the later window). [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The number of qualified items far exceeds what an unchanged process would produce (34 control-flow items against about 0.55 expected, 3 time items against about 0.02), so the differences as a whole are not a sampling artefact. The evidence supports the possibility that the five-activity block A30, A31, A36, A37, A38 swapped places with A22 and A21: in the earlier window the flow ran A20 → one of the block (with looping inside the block) → A22 → A21 → A25, whereas in the later window it runs A20 → A22 → A21 → one of the block → A25. This rests on direct relational evidence (all ten measured pairs flip from block-first to A21/A22-first), consistent position shifts, and consistent successor changes at A20, A21 and all five block activities, while participation is unchanged (each activity in 200 of 200 traces in both windows), ruling out activities appearing, disappearing or a mere shift in how often existing paths are taken. Limitations: the later-window lag profiles rest on one trace each, the A22→A21 connection is inferred from positions rather than a measured transition, and the internal order within the block is only partially observed, so an additional change inside the block cannot be ruled out; whether the block moved later or A22/A21 moved earlier is behaviourally indistinguishable here. [DIR001–DIR007, POS001–POS007, REL001–REL010, LAG001–LAG010]

Other differences: A timing change in its own right — the elapsed time between consecutive completions dropped by about half for A09→A10 and A11→A10 (the two pairs share A10 and may reflect one underlying change) and was nearly eliminated for A24→A28; these activities lie outside the reordered block, and the evidence does not show whether this timing change is connected to the reordering. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003]
